title: What Your Procrastination Is Protecting
description: Putting something off is usually avoidance of a feeling rather than a shortage of discipline. This worksheet helps you find the feeling, then take one small step anyway.
intro_md: There is no score here and no verdict about your character. Delay is information. The useful question is not “why am I so lazy” but “what does starting this make me feel, and what does putting it off protect me from?”

fields.label: The task, named as specifically as you can — not “sort my life out”, but the actual next action

title: Working With Intrusive Thoughts
description: A thought that arrives uninvited is not a plan, a wish, or a confession. This worksheet helps you notice one, step back from it, and decide what you do next.
intro_md: Intrusive thoughts are common — most people have them. They tend to run opposite to what you actually want, which is exactly why they alarm you. The aim here is not to work out what a thought means, or to argue it away. It is to let it be there without letting it steer. If a thought involves hurting yourself or someone else, or you cannot put it down, please talk to someone — in the US you can call or text 988 at any time.

fields.label: What you were doing when it arrived (time of day, where you were, who was around)
The thought, in a few words — a short phrase is enough, you do not need to write it out in full

Write it again starting with “I'm having the thought that…” — then read both versions and notice the difference
Name the shape of it without arguing with it (a doubt, a what-if, a worst-case image, an urge to check)
